title: Terrain and Friction: Surfaces, Slopes, and What the Ground Lets a Vehicle Do

questions.question: What decides the most force a tyre can put on the ground?
options: The weight on it times the friction coefficient
questions.explanation: No motor can push harder than the ground allows.

questions.question: At 2 m/s, ice against tarmac made the stopping distance:
questions.explanation: The distance goes as the inverse of the friction.

questions.question: Going down a grade of 0.2 on gravel, the stop from 2 m/s took:
options: 0.717 m, against 0.416 m on the flat

questions.question: Gravel can be climbed up to about:
questions.explanation: tan(angle) = mu minus the rolling resistance.

questions.question: Why is a speed limit set on a dry floor not safe on gravel?
options: The stopping distance goes as the inverse of the friction
Gravel is slippery only at night
questions.explanation: The limit has to follow the ground.
